what: Realtime sync keeps one shared document - a canvas, a doc, a board - identical on every device while several people (or an AI agent) edit it. A server room holds the authoritative copy and relays changes; CRDT libraries let edits merge without conflicts.
like: Like a shared whiteboard in a classroom where everyone's marker strokes appear on every copy instantly, and nobody's stroke wipes out anyone else's.
why: Learner, tutor agent and other devices see the same board at the same moment
History is kept, so a session can be replayed step by step

steps.d: Every canvas gets exactly one server room. tldraw.com runs each room in its own Cloudflare Durable Object, which also gives it a WebSocket server.
Each browser applies edits to its local copy instantly, then sends them to the room over a WebSocket.

steps.t: The agent is just another editor
steps.d: The tutor agent's typed canvas actions go through the same room, so its shapes appear on every device like a person's would.
The room saves snapshots (SQLite in production) and sends big binaries such as images to an asset store like R2.
The room relays each change to every other client; a client that reconnects resumes from the room's state.

numbers.l: TLSocketRoom per document, as tldraw requires
idle time after which a hibernating Cloudflare room snapshots sessions

choices.d: A server room (tldraw sync) keeps one source of truth and simple permissions; pure CRDTs (Yjs) also merge peer-to-peer and offline, at the cost of harder access control.
Durable Objects give one addressable instance per room with storage attached; on Node you run one room per document yourself.
tldraw's docs say auth, authorisation, rate limits and upload size limits are yours to add.
Client and server register the same custom shapes with migrations, so old and new clients can share a room.

instead.why: A plain socket server for broadcasts if there is no shared document to merge
For ordered messages rather than a shared editable state

breaks.d: Load balancing sends clients of the same canvas to different servers.
breaks.see: Edits appear on some devices and not others
breaks.fix: Route by room id to exactly one instance (Durable Object per room)

breaks.d: The template has no auth by default.
breaks.fix: Check a signed token for the room before accepting the socket
Shape migrations; ask old clients to refresh

say: Each session's canvas is one sync room - a Durable Object - holding the authoritative copy, persisting to SQLite and relaying changes over WebSockets.
The tutor agent writes to the same room through typed actions, so its drawings appear on every device and land in the history for replay.
I add a token check on join and rate limits, which the template leaves to me.

followups.q: Why not let the agent write straight to the database?
followups.a: Clients only see changes that go through the room; writing around it breaks sync and history. The agent is just another editor of the room.

followups.q: How do you replay a lesson?
followups.a: Room history plus the event log and audio timestamps let you scrub the canvas in step with the transcript.

today: Canvas SDKs now ship sync on serverless rooms: tldraw sync runs each room in a Cloudflare Durable Object with SQLite storage, and its agent starter kit streams AI edits through the same room.

check.q: How many server rooms should hold one tldraw document?
d: As many as the load balancer picks
check.why: One authoritative room per document keeps everyone in sync.

check.q: Where do large images on the canvas go?
check.a: An asset store such as R2
check.why: Big binaries go to asset storage; the room syncs references.

check.q: The tutor agent wants to draw. Best path?
check.a: Typed actions through the same sync room
d: Draw only on the learner's screen locally
check.why: Going through the room keeps every device and the history consistent.
